name: flaggems_cudnn_batch_norm_backward
description: cudnn_batch_norm_backward: batch-norm backward. Reference is the vendor aten.native_batch_norm_backward oracle with upcast inputs (mirrors the FlagGems correctness test); save_mean/save_var are the biased channel statistics of the input.
reference:
import torch

_STR2DTYPE = {
    "float16": torch.float16,
    "float32": torch.float32,
    "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16,
}


def gen_inputs(ctx, device):
    shape = tuple(ctx["input__shape"])
    dtype = _STR2DTYPE[ctx["input__dtype"]]
    C = shape[1]
    inp = torch.randn(shape, dtype=dtype, device=device)
    weight = torch.ones((C,), dtype=dtype, device=device)
    inp_f32 = inp.to(torch.float32)
    dims = [0] + list(range(2, inp.ndim))
    save_mean = inp_f32.mean(dim=dims).to(dtype)
    save_var = inp_f32.var(dim=dims, unbiased=False).to(dtype)
    grad_output = torch.ones_like(inp)
    reserve_space = torch.empty(0, dtype=dtype, device=device)
    return {
        "input": inp,
        "grad_output": grad_output,
        "weight": weight,
        "save_mean": save_mean,
        "save_var": save_var,
        "reserve_space": reserve_space,
    }


def run(input, grad_output, weight, running_mean, running_var, save_mean, save_var, eps, reserve_space):
    return torch.ops.aten.cudnn_batch_norm_backward(
        input,
        grad_output,
        weight,
        running_mean,
        running_var,
        save_mean,
        save_var,
        eps,
        reserve_space,
    )


def run_correctness(input, grad_output, weight, running_mean, running_var, save_mean, save_var, eps, reserve_space):
    ref_save_invstd = torch.rsqrt(save_var.float() + eps)
    in_grad, weight_grad, bias_grad = torch.ops.aten.native_batch_norm_backward(
        grad_output.float(),
        input.float(),
        weight.float() if weight is not None else None,
        None,
        None,
        save_mean.float(),
        ref_save_invstd,
        True,
        eps,
        [True, True, True],
    )
    return (
        in_grad.to(input.dtype),
        weight_grad.to(weight.dtype),
        bias_grad.to(grad_output.dtype),
    )
